title: Fourier weight bound for matching labelings
statement: Let $r,k,n$ be nonnegative integers with $n>0$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ have all its nonzero Fourier coefficients supported on subsets of size $k$. In the complete $2r$-partite graph with $k$ vertices in each part, sum over all perfect matchings and vertex labelings by $[n]$ that are constant on each matched edge the product, over the parts, of the absolute Fourier coefficient indexed by the set of labels in that part. This sum is at most the number of perfect matchings times $(k!)^r$ times the $r$th power of the total squared Fourier weight on subsets of size $k$.
hypotheses_covered: Every nonzero Fourier coefficient of $f$ is indexed by a subset of size $k$
